subject: Auth spike detected — request to preserve telemetry and access logs
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: ops@fintegrity.com, Sara Nolan <sara.nolan@fintegrity.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Auth spike detected — request to preserve telemetry and access logs

Hi Sara / FinIntegrity ops team,

TL;DR: We observed a short-lived authentication spike impacting a subset of tokens for your tenant between 08:43–08:52 PT this morning. No persisted customer data was modified. As part of our IR playbook we want to request preservation of your side’s logs and confirm we can collect additional telemetry for forensic correlation.

What we observed (Redwood side):
- 08:43–08:48 PT: rapid succession of 401 responses from 12 ephemeral clients tied to your tenant ID; request rates peaked at ~120 req/min.
- 08:48–08:52 PT: token refresh attempts retried; our gateway returned throttling for ~30s while backend auth issuers rotated keys.
- No successful privilege escalation or data exfiltration detected.

Actions we are taking:
- We rotated transient tokens used by the affected pool and flagged the session set for monitoring.
- Forensics team has captured a telemetry snapshot and a sanitized CSV we can share.
- We are preparing a short postmortem and follow-up remediation steps.

What we request from you (please preserve for now):
1) Access logs (auth logs/token issuance) for tenant finintegrity-prod between 2028-02-20 08:30–09:30 PT.
2) Any perimeter gateway/IDS alerts or blocklists covering the same window.
3) Any manual changes to auth providers or key rotations initiated from your side in that period.

Preservation instructions attached as a brief text file (preservation-instructions.txt). Please do not purge or rotate logs for the requested window until we confirm collection.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min call to walk through the artifacts — suggested times below.

Thanks — trying to be proactive here.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Security PM | Redwood Inference
[attachment: preservation-instructions.txt (text, 1.2KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fintegrity.com, Sara Nolan <sara.nolan@fintegrity.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Auth spike detected — request to preserve telemetry and access logs

Hannah — thanks for the quick note. A couple of internal asks to coordinate with the customer: 

- Karthik: can we prepare the SOC2-relevant packet for this event (logs, timeline, who touched keys) so we can provide the customer an evidence bundle if they need to file? Preferably redacted for PI.
- Neha: please pull the SIG/CAIQ crosswalk entries that map this class of auth event to our control responses; customer compliance teams often want the mapping.

Suggested customer-facing deliverables (we should confirm with FinIntegrity):
1) Short incident summary (one page) + timeline (we can produce this by EOD).
2) Forensics snapshot CSV (sanitized) — safe to share.
3) Evidence list for SOC2 (control IDs, retention windows, who was involved).

Hannah: when you share the postmortem, include the suggested retention window and a small checklist they can drop into their evidence repository. Also add a link to the boxed Drive folder where we'll place artifacts (see JIRA-4321 referenced).

Marissa
Head of Security Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nolan <sara.nolan@fintegrity.com>, ops@fintegrity.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Final postmortem and artifact package — auth spike (2028-02-20)

Hi Sara — following up with the closure package. Thank you and your ops team for preserving the requested logs while we collected telemetry. Attached are:

- redwood-ir-postmortem.pdf (formal one-page postmortem + action items)
- forensics-telemetry-snippet.csv (sanitized request-level rows for 08:43–08:52 PT)
- preservation-instructions.txt (original ask for reference)

Summary (short):
- Root cause: transient mismatch during automated key rotation between our auth issuer and a small fraction of issued tokens causing a validation flap.
- Impact: brief authentication failures for ~0.8% of your requests for ~9 minutes; no data access beyond normal product usage.
- Remediation: improved pre-rotation validation, extra health check before key swap, and an expanded alert for token validation error rates.

Attached artifacts: [attachment: redwood-ir-postmortem.pdf (PDF, 45KB)], [attachment: forensics-telemetry-snippet.csv (CSV, 18KB)], [attachment: preservation-instructions.txt (text, 1.2KB)].

Next steps / ask of FinIntegrity:
- Confirm receipt and that preserved logs may now be rotated (reply with OK to this thread).
- If your compliance team needs a SOC2/CLA-style evidence packet, let us know and we’ll produce a redacted bundle mapped to control IDs; Marissa is the lead for that.
- Optional follow-up tabletop: we can run a 45-min joint tabletop review of the timeline and updated playbook in the next 2 weeks.

If you want the Drive folder link directly, use: https://drive.google.com/drive/fakeid-preservation (we've placed the artifacts there).

Appreciate the quick coordination — happy to hop on a call.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Security PM | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-ir-postmortem.pdf (PDF, 45KB)]
